question: Can the published metric be reproduced under the same physical and evaluation model?
audience: Researchers assessing decoder failure across noise conditions
baseline: Transformer on identical simulation inputs; retain both with- and without-latency-noise conditions

settings.released_data: author simulated real-time outcomes, distances 3 to 9
settings.noise_injection: four decoder-latency-dependent noise injections in 28-round simulations
settings.replay_definition: Compare actual and predicted final observable bits with/without injected noise. This reanalyzes released data, not training or hardware Figure 2.

hypothesis: The registered metric can be matched under the original protocol; no predicted advantage in the qkp simulator is asserted.
decision_rule: Compare independently measured estimates and uncertainty with reported values or marked visual-reading ranges. A match is provisional until model, split and units are audited; missing code/data or imprecise estimates remain inconclusive. Do not tune on held-out test data.
compute: Smoke: CPU, one thread, small bounded input. Production: explicitly launch after resolving listed blockers; no full training is started by fetch/check.
uncertainty: Wilson intervals for independent Bernoulli counts; bootstrap trajectory/seed-level fits for lifetimes and thresholds. Use three independent training seeds for new training, reported separately.
procedure: Replay the released actual/predicted observable files for both architectures and noise-injection conditions. Export errors, shots and Wilson intervals. To regenerate observations or reproduce hardware per-round targets, obtain the author model and training implementation. Do not use the preprint threshold to label the accepted article benchmark.
blockers: Author training/decoder code is withheld for intellectual-property reasons; available on request.
Public repository releases numerical real-time data, not the hardware model or training code.
Replay results are shot failure rates and must not be compared directly to hardware per-round targets.
raw_output_contract: See ../RESULTS.md. Save raw outcomes, checkpoint/config/source hashes, environment, seed and noise units.
